chunks: And from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

Indeed, Allah (Glorious is His Majesty) apologizes to His destitute servant who was in this world, just as a brother apologizes to his brother, saying: 'By My Might and My Glory, I did not impoverish you for a slightness/disgrace that was upon Me from you. So raise this veil and look at what I have compensated you with from this world.' So the veil is lifted for him and he sees what Allah (Glorious is His Majesty) has compensated him with from this world, so he says: 'I have not been harmed, O Lord, given what You have given me in exchange.'

key_terms.الْغِطَاءَ: The veil or covering, referring to the unseen reality of divine compensation.
key_terms.الْمَحُوجِ: The destitute or one in need, referring to a believer who experienced poverty or hardship.
key_terms.عَوَّضْتُكَ: I have compensated you, referring to the spiritual or eternal rewards given in exchange for worldly loss.
key_terms.لَيَعْتَذِرُ: He apologizes or explains himself, indicating a gentle, non-punitive reason for the hardship.
key_terms.مَا ضَرَّنِي: I have not been harmed, expressing the believer's realization that the loss was negligible compared to the gain.

ai.seo_question: Why did Allah make a believer poor in this world according to the hadith of Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith describes Allah's apology to a believer who suffered poverty or hardship in this world, clarifying that it was not a punishment for their insignificance but a test. Upon entering the afterlife, the believer sees the immense compensation provided by Allah and realizes that the worldly hardship caused no real harm compared to the divine reward.
